sources.entry: stretchly - Cross-platform electron app that reminds you to take breaks when working with computer.

summary.one_liner: Stretchly is a cross-platform Electron app that runs in the tray and reminds you to take short and long breaks from computer work.
summary.what_it_does: Stretchly sits in the system tray and schedules Mini breaks (default 20 seconds every 10 minutes) and Long breaks (default 5 minutes every 30 minutes after two Mini breaks). It shows a notification before each break and a full break window with a countdown and a break idea. Breaks can be postponed or skipped, with a configurable postpone limit and time. It pauses breaks when the system is idle, when Do Not Disturb is on, and optionally when listed programs run or on suspend/lock. Most settings are available in a Preferences window, and the rest are edited in a JSON preferences file. A command-line interface (`stretchly help`) can control a running instance.
use_cases: remind me to take regular breaks from the computer
reduce eye strain and sitting time during work
pause break reminders during meetings or fullscreen apps
customize break intervals and break ideas
run break timers across macOS, Windows and Linux
how_to_run: git clone the repository, then run: npm install
notable: Idle detection and Do Not Disturb monitoring that pause breaks automatically
Strict mode, manual finish mode and global keyboard shortcuts for postpone, skip and pause
Custom break ideas with limited HTML and local images, plus custom WAV sounds
Command-line control of a running instance, including starting the last break again
Pause or resume breaks based on which programs are running (appExclusions)
caveats: macOS builds are only ad-hoc signed, so first launch needs a Gatekeeper workaround
Several Linux and Wayland issues are listed, such as global shortcuts on KDE Wayland and multi-monitor placement
Many advanced options require hand-editing the JSON preferences file, and the README warns some may break the app
